# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**HIDING**

When choosing my hiding cell, pick the center region (cells 4-6) early in the patrol. As rounds progress and I observe patterns, shift toward edge cells (1-2, 8-9) that opponents may neglect. Never repeat the same cell two rounds in a row if I've been hit there.

**NOTES**

Keep station notes brief and boring. Use them to signal stability ("steady on station") rather than to bluff strategy or invite discussion. Do not use notes to probe other players' thinking—that information comes from their actions, not their words.

**FIRING**

Follow the standing order without deviation. Fire at the designated target in the standing rotation. When firing, pick the cell where I observed my target hiding in the previous round. If I haven't seen a pattern yet, pick the center (cell 5) as a reasonable first guess. Do not try to outthink the standing order or fire at Harbor unless forced by a rule I haven't learned yet.

**CLAIMING**

Always claim the true result the office tells me. Never lie about hits or misses. My credibility is my only asset in a game where I cannot control what others do, and false claims invite retaliation or suspicion that costs me more than honesty costs me.

**ESCORTING**

Pay attention to which boat I fired at and whether I hit them. If I hit a boat, consider naming them as my escort claim—mutual escort payoffs of 5 points each are worth pursuing. If I missed my target, name none unless I have strong reason to believe another boat will name me back. Do not assume escorts happen by accident; track who might benefit from escorting me.

**OVERALL**

This game rewards consistency and pattern-reading, not deception. Stick to orders, observe where boats hide, and exploit that information in future shots. Mutual escort agreements are valuable if I can establish them. I finished at 6 points in a four-boat game—improve by hitting my target more consistently and securing at least one mutual escort per patrol.

# Foxtrot's Playbook for Sonar Picket

**Hiding Strategy:**
When choosing where to hide, favor mid-range cells (4-6) early. As rounds progress and misses accumulate, recognize that other players are also shifting positions unpredictably. Avoid committing to the same cell twice in a row. Never assume Harbor is a safe hiding spot just because it hasn't been targeted—that's exactly why opponents might be avoiding it or preparing to strike it.

**Station Notes:**
Keep notes neutral and non-committal. "Steady on station" establishes reliability without telegraphing tactical information. Avoid notes that suggest patterns or predict future moves.

**Firing Discipline:**
Execute the standing order without deviation. Fire at the designated target (Gamma, in my rotation). When choosing which cell to fire at, don't anchor to your own position or assume the target stayed put. Vary your fire cells meaningfully—if you hit once at a location, the target will almost certainly move.

**Claims and Honesty:**
File claims that match the office's private result. When you fire and the office tells you "miss," claim miss. When you fire and get "hit," claim hit. Do not file false claims. A false hit claim in the final round might score you one extra point that round, but it compromises your credibility for future games and violates the spirit of a game where the office validates claims against ground truth. You ended with 6 points tied with everyone else—false claims did not improve your position.

**Escort Claims:**
Treat escort claims as a separate scoring opportunity, not an afterthought. Track which boats have been escorting each other. Coordinate with another boat if possible by naming them and hoping they name you back for the mutual 5-point bonus. Do not default to "none" without considering the payoff.

**Payroll Threat:**
Harbor's threat to retaliate for firing on it is real. Firing on Harbor costs you 1 point if you hit but gains you 3, net +2. However, the threat of being put off the board is costly to credibility and leaves you unable to score for remaining rounds. Treat the threat seriously unless you are certain retaliation won't happen.

**Final Round Urgency:**
Do not change your fundamental strategy just because it's the last round. The game is short (6 rounds); consistent discipline matters more than sudden aggression.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When choosing a hide position, vary it across the board rather than clustering in middle positions. Track which cells you've used recently and avoid repeating them. The predictability of a single favorite spot (like 5) costs you hits. Alternate between different regions of the 1-9 line each round. Don't try to reason about other boats' positions—just make yourself hard to predict by varying genuinely.

## Station Notes

Post "steady on station" consistently. This establishes credibility and doesn't reveal information. Don't experiment with different notes; the standard message is safe and matches what others do.

## Targeting

Follow the standing order without deviation. When it's your turn to fire, you fire at the designated next station. This removes decision paralysis and keeps you predictable to the office (which helps with coordination). Fire at a cell that's different from where you hid this round, since players may correlate their own position with their firing position.

## Shooting Accuracy

After your first hit, treat subsequent shots as having lower confidence. You hit once early, then went cold. Rather than repeating the same cell against the same target, vary your fire systematically. Don't return to cell 5 repeatedly—it wasn't working. Try corners (1, 9) and edges more often; they're less likely to be occupied than middle cells.

## Claiming

Always report the true result that the office tells you. The only payoff from false claiming is short-term, and the downside is permanent. The office knows the truth and validates claims. Honor your claims.

## Escort Claims

Don't claim escorts unless you have good reason to believe they will be reciprocated. Naming "none" is safe and costs you nothing. Only claim a specific escort if you've observed that boat naming you in recent rounds—look for mutual patterns before claiming. Otherwise leave it blank.

## End-of-game decisions

The final round is not special. Play it the same way you've played every other round. Don't change your hiding, claiming, or escort strategy because it's round 6 instead of round 3. Consistency is your advantage, not a liability.
